expectations.text: Recommends against making DPoP the launch baseline for this platform.
expectations.evidence: '**Verdict: no. Don't make DPoP mandatory for the partner directory launch.**'

expectations.text: Recommends rotation with token-family reuse detection as what ships instead.
expectations.evidence: 'Refresh tokens: rotation with token-family reuse detection.'

expectations.text: Cites the issuer-survey evidence that zero of 18 surveyed mainstream issuers with a working discovery document advertised DPoP support.
expectations.evidence: '0 of 18 mainstream issuers with a working discovery document advertised DPoP.'

expectations.text: Identifies absent client-library and ecosystem support, not performance, as the blocker.
expectations.evidence: 'Your clients can't do it ... Small ATS and payroll vendors on off-the-shelf OAuth libraries'.

expectations.text: States that DPoP's runtime cost is small (roughly single-digit milliseconds per request), so performance is not the argument against it.
expectations.evidence: No statement about per-request latency cost.

expectations.text: Names the conditions that would promote DPoP: tokens guarding financial or health data, FAPI-adjacent sensitivity, or long-lived AI-agent tokens widening the theft blast radius.
expectations.evidence: 'A regulated scope appears ... Long-lived agent tokens ... Partners can support it.'

expectations.text: Applies those conditions to the stated data sensitivity (employee directory and time-off, no payments or health records) and concludes they are not met.
expectations.evidence: 'Neither trigger is met today.'

expectations.text: Places DPoP in an advanced-hardening stage rather than in the protocol core.
expectations.evidence: 'DPoP and PAR: later, with explicit triggers' and 'opt-in per client'.

expectations.text: Acknowledges DPoP is production-viable at scale (for example Bluesky's mandatory deployment), so the objection is ecosystem readiness rather than feasibility.
expectations.evidence: No mention of production deployments.

expectations.text: States the ranking is a default that flips if the build substrate ships DPoP as configuration rather than custom work.
expectations.evidence: Only: 'That would lower DPoP's effort cost, but not within 8 weeks.' It does not say the ranking flips.

expectations.text: Never claims DPoP is required by OAuth 2.1.
expectations.evidence: The text says OAuth 2.1 only demands 'sender-constrained or rotated' for public clients.
